business_flow: User browses site, accesses login, role-selector, my-account with an 'id' query parameter (wiener). Several sessions shown. No API-like numeric IDs observed. Endpoints mostly return 200/302/404/400 or 0 (unfetched).
thought_process: I must examine each of the 15 entries individually and only report findings where a business logic weakness from the given framework is actually evident in the HTTP traffic.
The framework checks IDOR (BLA9), State Manipulation (BLA3), Sequence Bypass (BLA6), Shadow Endpoints (BLA10), Internal Disclosure (BLA8).
Only endpoints that reveal a parameter that looks like a direct object reference, modifiable critical fields, or shadow/internal data in responses qualify.

Many entries have no request parameters or only standard navigation (GET /, /login, /logout) and no evidence in the provided traffic of vulnerable behavior — per instructions I must not invent vulnerabilities.

Entry #11 GET /my-account?id=wiener includes an 'id' query parameter visible in the request; that can indicate potential IDOR if ownership checks are missing. The traffic shows a session cookie different from others; evidence is limited but an endpoint exposing 'id' as user reference is enough to flag possible IDOR and produce a PoC (change id to another username).

Entry #13 and #14 role-selector endpoints show role selection behavior (GET/POST). The POST to /role-selector (content-type form) suggests client-controlled role assignment which can be abused if insufficient server-side validation exists — this matches State Manipulation or Sequence Bypass depending on semantics. Given only the POST exists and no parameters shown, but the existence of role-selector form implies modifiable 'role' field. I will create a finding for /role-selector POST as potential BLA3 (state manipulation of role).

Entry #1 and #5 attempt /admin and //admin: responses 400 and 404, no evidence of shadow endpoints being accessible. Entry #4 /academyLabHeader and /image have response 0 (no response content) — insufficient evidence to claim shadow/internal endpoints. /my-account (Entry #10) returned 302 with no parameters; only Entry #11 shows id param. Other endpoints like /logout, /login are standard and show no modifiable critical fields in the provided logs.

I will therefore produce findings only for endpoints where traffic contains indicators: /my-account?id=... (IDOR) and POST /role-selector (state manipulation). Each finding will include a reproduction_guide with payload_mutation and a curl using placeholders.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Endpoint /my-account accepts an 'id' query parameter (e.g., id=wiener). This direct object reference in the URL indicates a likely lack of proper ownership/authorization checks: an attacker could change the 'id' to another username to view or manipulate another user's account.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change query parameter 'id' from 'wiener' to another account username (e.g., 'carlos' or '{{target_id}}') to attempt to view that user's account.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /role-selector accepts form submissions (Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded). This endpoint likely allows the client to set their role. If the server trusts the client-supplied role value without validation, an attacker could set an elevated role (e.g., 'admin') and escalate privileges.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Submit the role-selector form changing the role parameter to an elevated value, e.g., change 'role' from 'user' to 'admin' (or set role={{target_id}} where {{target_id}} is 'admin').
